summary:
## Project: Upgrading FRS Dashboard with 3M Carbon Fiber Wrap
This project replaces the scratched, faux carbon fiber plastic trim in a Scion FRS with a high-quality **3M DI-NOC carbon fiber vinyl wrap** for an improved aesthetic.

## Required Tools & Materials
* **Vinyl Wrap:** A **1 ft x 4 ft sheet** of 3M DI-NOC Carbon Fiber vinyl is sufficient for most dashboard jobs.
* **Cleaning:** **Rubbing alcohol** and a microfiber rag.
* **Cutting:** Scissors and a sharp **X-Acto knife**.
* **Application:** A **squeegee** and a **hairdryer** or heat gun.
* **Adhesion:** **3M Primer 94** adhesion promoter.
* **Disassembly:** Interior plastic pry tools.

## Step-by-Step Process

### 1. Preparation
* **Remove Trim:** Carefully use pry tools to remove the interior trim pieces from the dashboard.
* **Clean Surfaces:** The most critical step for good adhesion.
    * Thoroughly wipe down the **front and back** of each trim piece with rubbing alcohol to remove all oils, dust, and residue.
    * Wash your hands before handling the cleaned pieces to avoid transferring oils.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Just like painting, the quality of your vinyl wrap is determined by your prep work. A perfectly clean surface is essential for the vinyl to stick properly and last.

### 2. Alignment & Application
* **Pattern Continuity:** For multi-piece dashboards, lay the pieces on the vinyl sheet in their final orientation, leaving a small (~0.5 inch) gap between them. This ensures the **carbon fiber weave pattern** is continuous across the seam.
* **Initial Placement:** Carefully peel the backing paper and lay the trim pieces onto the adhesive side of the vinyl. Start by applying pressure to the center and work your way out.

### 3. Trimming and Wrapping Edges
* **Trim Excess:** Cut the vinyl around the piece, leaving a **0.5- to 1-inch margin** to wrap around the back.
* **Use Heat:** Gently use a hairdryer to heat the vinyl around edges and curves. This makes it more **flexible and pliable**, allowing it to stretch and conform without wrinkles.
* **Corners:** Make small **relief cuts** in the corners to help the vinyl lay flat when folded over.
* **Secure the Edges:** Apply **3M Primer 94** to the backside edges of the plastic trim. This acts as a powerful adhesion promoter, preventing the vinyl from peeling up over time.

> [!TIP]
> When in doubt, leave more excess vinyl than you think you need. It's always easier to trim more off later than to come up short.

## Key Takeaways & Warnings
* **3M Primer 94:** This product is extremely effective but has a very short working time.
    * Once the inner capsule is broken, you only have about **5-10 minutes** before it dries out.
    * It's recommended to buy a **three-pack** so you have spares and can work on each piece with a fresh applicator.
* **Heat Application:** A hairdryer is safer than a heat gun, as it's less likely to accidentally melt the plastic trim. Use just enough heat to make the vinyl stretchy.
* **Pattern Alignment:** The biggest challenge for multi-piece trims is maintaining the pattern. Plan your layout before you peel the vinyl backing.
